extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, Royal Society members, physicians and early scientists reading Philosophical Transactions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and exemplars for writing and reporting observational natural-history and medical case reports (specimen descriptions, locality, experimental tests, and claims of priority) as in 17th‑century Philosophical Transactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming priority of discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements about who first found or demonstrated a result (dates of discovery vs publication), and whether a later printed work should prejudice an earlier discoverer's claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate priority by evidence of actual earlier discovery or demonstration (not just print date). Private communication dates, earlier demonstrations, knowledge by many, and related prior propositions (e.g., Dr. Wallis's Schol. prop. 38) can establish precedence. Do not let later print-publication automatically override credible earlier discovery; consider demonstrations, communications, and contemporaneous acknowledgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical case report content (stones in bladder example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include patient age, symptoms and course (duration, nature of pain, urinary symptoms), findings at dissection, counts and measurements of stones, weights, shapes, textures, and presence/absence in related organs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give precise quantities (number of stones, weight of largest/least, total weight), qualitative descriptions (triangular/quadrangular, worn flats, blunted corners, compact matter like white clay), and negative findings (no sign in kidneys/ureters). Note causal observations (opening at bladder orifice causing death). Indicate provenance/translator when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describing malformed foetus / anatomical anomalies
rubrics_metrics.description: Report external form, apparent vitality, specific deformities (absent forehead, eye placement, skull structure), and internal anatomy findings (presence/absence of brain, bone form and attachments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide careful macroscopic description (colour, resemblance to known structures), dissection observations (hollow vs solid cranium, continuity of marrow with head), and interpretation (how the anatomy might explain observed life/death events). Note context (when seen, who observed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimen locality and contextual information
rubrics_metrics.description: For natural curiosities, state where specimens were collected, local environmental context (e.g., coral-fishing in the channel of Messina), and immediate handling/experimentation (squeezing, immersion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report collector/presenter, precise locality, method of collection/observation, and any immediate field tests (feel under water vs in air). Record temporal aspects (change after being drawn from sea; time to change taste ~six hours).

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical and chemical tests for substance identification (coral, salts, bitumen, sal ammoniac)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use sensory tests (taste, smell), mechanical tests (flexibility when fresh, brittleness after exposure), heating/burning (bituminous smell on burning), dissolution and sublimation (salt of coral dissolved and coagulated on evaporation; sal ammoniac sublimed from burnt minerals), and reaction with reagents (vinegar corrodes fossils; spirit of vitriol, aqua fortis corrode calculi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe procedures and outcomes (e.g., coral juice is milky and acrimonious when fresh; dries and changes colour in ~6 hours). Use these tests to argue mineral vs vegetable origin or factitious origin. Record comparative behaviours (hinders ignition of sulphur and nitre).

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental reproduction as evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Where possible, attempt to reproduce or simulate formation (e.g., show a 'salt of coral' which on dissolution and gentle evaporation coagulates into small sticks resembling a forest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reproducible laboratory manipulations to support a hypothesis about origin (factitious vs natural). Report methods, observations, and inferences connecting the experiment to natural occurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphological description of invertebrates (sanguisuga / leech)
rubrics_metrics.description: Record dimensions (length ~4 inches), body features (belly white, cartilaginous, transparent), presence/absence of head/eyes, specialized structures (hollow snout with hard membrane), tail shape (feather-like), filaments for attachment, and internal structures (vessels resembling guts used for suction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain observed feeding mechanics (pumping action, snout as sucker), ecological interactions (attacked areas of host not reachable by fins), and note parasites on specimens (a louse attached to the leech). Provide comparative references to literature (Gesner, Johnston).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting mineral/organic distillation and fractionation (fungus/mineral juice example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe sample source (location and depth), physical appearance (peat-like, clammy, jelly-like pieces, bituminous lumps), and results of distillation fractions (acidulous limpid water, white liquor, yellow oil like amber/pitch).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record techniques (distillation), yields, and interpretations about origin (vegetable vs fossil bitumen) while acknowledging uncertainty. Compare to known substances and historical sources (Pliny).

rubrics_metrics.name: Description and classification of figured stones (trochitae and entrochi)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detail shape (cylindrical single joints), surface features (flat smooth circle, rays from central hole), jointing (how rays interlock, sutures indented or apparent), size ranges (from pin-head to ~2 inches), thickness, and state (broken fragments, beds in rock, dislocation/distortion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note variation across localities (Braughton, Stock, Staffordshire), reaction to reagents (vinegar dissolves when broken into grains), and hypothesize on growth/formation (affinity to rock-plants/corals). Include numbered figure explanations to support morphological distinctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptive completeness for specimen reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide multiple axes of description: quantitative measures (size, thickness, counts), qualitative morphology (rays, sutures, edges), state of preservation (broken, depressed, twisted), material properties (polished, shining, opaque), and geological context (beds, rock hardness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare specimens, report variability, include localities and occurrences, and supply illustrative figures or plates where possible to communicate forms precisely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of books and contributions (book-account examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess works for originality, usefulness, and whether further analysis is necessary (e.g., a well-known book of physicians may render a new analysis superfluous).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value comprehensive prefaces tracing origin/progress of field, detailed instrument descriptions (as in Hevelius), and whether observations or data are reserved for subsequent volumes. Reprinting decisions weigh importance and novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducible procedural reporting (volatile salt extraction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide step-by-step process details: selection of material (leaves in warm weather), preparation (pressing into heap until pappy), formation into pellets, distillation in glass retort, separation of oil and liquor, and rectifications to obtain volatile spirit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record conditions (warm weather), expected intermediate products (thick black oil, liquor), and sensory comparisons (spirit indistinguishable by smell/taste from hartshorn, blood, urine, or sal ammoniac). Ensure enough procedural detail for reproduction.
